newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Norilsk says strike may kill repayment plan.
newsitem.headline: Russia Norilsk says strike may kill repayment plan.

text.p: Management at Russia's Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS views any labour strike at the firm's flagship plant as a move that could scupper a repayment schedule for salary and holiday arrears, a Norilsk spokesman said on Friday.

"If production at the plant is normal and workers fulfill monthly output and do not impede sales, we (the management) will carry out our plan of paying off arrears (to workers)," Moscow-based Norilsk spokesman Anatoly Komrakov said on Friday.

An appeal body of three legislative (elected) Norilsk town officials decided on Thursday that the arrears repayment schedule could be only fulfilled if there was no halt to output or sales at the flagship combine, a Norilsk statement said.

Komrakov said the appeal body was independent and that its decisions were not legally binding under Russian law and were only recommendations -- but he said that management was adhering to the body's decision.
A reconciliation commission grouping representatives of management and labour had turned to the body and asked it to take a decision on the arrears issue.
Norilsk union representatives could not immediately be reached for comment and there was no information on whether labour would abide by the body's decisions.
The appeal body decided that the repayment schedule was realistic, the statement said. The body also stressed the need for the two sides to resolve the dispute by negotiations only.
Norilsk management has said it can repay the debt over 1997.
Management and labour are due to meet on Saturday in the Arctic town of Norilsk where the flagship plant is situated.

Norilsk Nickel group general director Alexander Khloponin, who is also a board member of commercial bank Uneximbank, is expected to take part. Uneximbank holds 38 percent, or 51 percent of the voting shares in RAO Norilsky Nickel,
Komrakov said the body's findings would be discussed at the meeting.
"I hope the union's reaction to the findings will be normal," he said.
The United Trade Union committee, representing mining and refining workers, said on Wednesday it might call a strike on March 15 over wage and holiday arrears.
Salary arrears and overdue holiday payments to workers at the flagship plant are 900 billion roubles, and the Norilsk group also owes about 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets.
The Norilsk statement said more financing could come from transferring unspecified company-financed "social property" to the city.

Norilsk management has said it spent 4.5 trillion roubles last year -- nearly 42 percent of its 1996 revenues -- on supporting social infrastructure and social spending in Norilsk, which is 200 km north of the Arctic Circle.

A Communications Ministry spokesman said telephone lines between Moscow and Norilsk, which are sometimes of poor quality, were not working on Friday and could give no indication of when they might be operational.
An unidentified Norilsk official said Moscow-based Norilsk officials and spokesman would not be available on Saturday for comment on the talks.
Norilsk is a major supplier of nickel, cobalt and platinum group metals to world markets.
--Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
